title: Whole-system reduction of the datum pullback compositor
statement: Fix D,C,E,n,S,o,z and invertibility of the coefficient prime [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. For composable finite-type-space arrows f:X -> Y and g:Y -> Z and constructible N on Z, let chi be pullComparison [def-sf-integral-proper-projection-coordinates]. Reduction of S.higher.integral.pullComposition(f,g) at N, followed by chi_f at pull_g N and system pull_f of chi_g at N, equals chi_(f followed by g) at N followed by z.compositors.pullComp(f,g) at reduce_Z N. This is solely a pullback equation: tensor, open extension and projection do not occur.

proof.text: Compose the datum finite coefficient comparison with the finitePullback realization. Naturality of finitePullback moves the inner comparison past the outer pullback. The pullComposition equation of integralNormalization.reduction and finitePullCompositionNormalization then give the canonical intrinsic finite compositor square.

proof.text: Apply integralProjectionPullEvaluation to each of f, g and their composite, and cancel its finitePullback inverse. This identifies evaluation of pullComparison followed by the intrinsic pullback-evaluation map with reductionEvaluation followed by the finite coefficient comparison. Reverse systemPullbackCompositorEvaluation by cancelling its isomorphisms to obtain the forward system-compositor evaluation square.

proof.text: Postcompose the desired evaluated square with the two pullback-evaluation isomorphisms and the iterated finite pullback of reductionEvaluation at N. Naturality of outer pullback evaluation, the three unary equations, naturality of reductionEvaluation, and the finite datum-compositor square reduce it to the forward system-compositor evaluation equation. Cancel this common invertible postcomposition.

proof.text: On X the coefficient prime is invertible in every residue field, so whole-system reduction restricted to constructible integral objects is full. Lift the system compositor, conjugated by pullComparison, to an integral arrow b. The preceding evaluated square and the lift equation show that reduction of the datum compositor and reduction of b have equal finite evaluations. Naturality of reductionEvaluation and faithfulness of the finite full-subcategory inclusion turn these into equality under every actual finite integral reduction. Apply integral_reductions_jointly_faithful to the two integral arrows, then apply whole-system reduction and cancel the conjugating isomorphisms. This proves the original system equation without claiming that arbitrary derived evaluations are faithful.

lean.statement:
theorem integralDatumPullCompositionReduction
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) (hl : IsUnit (C.l : D.k))
    (o : Operations C.l E) (z : Realizations C.l E D o)
    {X Y Z : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (N : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E Z.obj.left) :
    (reduce X).map ((S.higher.integral.pullComposition f g).hom.app N) ≫
        (pullComparison S.higher hl o z f).hom.app ((S.higher.integral.pull g).obj N) ≫
        (pull C.l E f.hom.left).map ((pullComparison S.higher hl o z g).hom.app N) =
      (pullComparison S.higher hl o z (f ≫ g)).hom.app N ≫
        (z.compositors.pullComp f.hom.left g.hom.left).hom.app ((reduce Z).obj N)
